nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $b$ a list of bits with one bit per vertex pair, that is, with as many entries as the list of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$. Then for every Boolean predicate $P$ on a pair of natural numbers and a bit, $P$ holds on every entry of the pair list zipped with $b$ (the $t$-th pair together with the $t$-th bit of $b$) if and only if, for all natural numbers $i < j < n$, $P$ holds on the…
nodes.title: Checking each listed vertex pair against its bit

nodes.summary: For every bit string $x$, $x$ is in CLIQUE if and only if there is a bit string $w$ of length at most the length of $x$ such that the shared CLIQUE / INDEPENDENT-SET / VERTEX-COVER verifier, run in clique mode, accepts the input $x$ with witness $w$.
nodes.title: CLIQUE is verified with witnesses no longer than the input

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a list of bits $b$, the graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ read off $b$ has a clique of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if there is a set $s$ of exactly $k$ of these vertices meeting the clique-mode pair condition on every pair $i < j$: whenever $i$ and $j$ both lie in $s$, the bit of the pair $\{i, j\}$ in $b$ is set.
nodes.title: Cliques of the graph given by pair bits

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every function $f$ from $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to the Booleans, the number of entries equal to true in the list $f(0), f(1), \dots, f(n-1)$ equals the number of indices $i < n$ with $f(i)$ true.
nodes.title: Counting the set bits of a list built from a function

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a list of bits $b$, the graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ read off $b$ has a vertex cover of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if there is a set $s$ of exactly $k$ of these vertices meeting the cover-mode pair condition on every pair $i < j$: whenever the bit of the pair $\{i, j\}$ in $b$ is set, $i$ or $j$ lies in $s$.
nodes.title: Vertex covers of the graph given by pair bits

nodes.summary: Fix a mode (clique, independent set or vertex cover) and bit strings $x$ and $w$. If the verifier in that mode accepts the input $x$ with witness $w$, then there are natural numbers $k$ and $n$ and a list of bits $b$ such that $x$ is the encoding of the instance $(k, n, b)$, $b$ has exactly one bit per vertex pair $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$, and some set of exactly $k$ of the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ meets the…
nodes.title: An accepted input encodes an instance with a good vertex set

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $R$ a relation on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $R(i, j)$ implies $R(j, i)$. Then $R(i, j)$ holds for all $i \ne j$ if and only if $R(i, j)$ holds for all $i < j$.
nodes.title: Symmetric relations on increasing pairs

nodes.summary: For every bit string $x$, $x$ is in INDEPENDENT-SET if and only if there is a bit string $w$ of length at most the length of $x$ such that the shared CLIQUE / INDEPENDENT-SET / VERTEX-COVER verifier, run in independent-set mode, accepts the input $x$ with witness $w$.
nodes.title: INDEPENDENT-SET is verified with witnesses no longer than the input

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a list of bits $b$, the graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ read off $b$ has an independent set of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if there is a set $s$ of exactly $k$ of these vertices meeting the independent-set-mode pair condition on every pair $i < j$: whenever $i$ and $j$ both lie in $s$, the bit of the pair $\{i, j\}$ in $b$ is not set.
nodes.title: Independent sets of the graph given by pair bits

nodes.summary: The verifier machine for CLIQUE, INDEPENDENT-SET and VERTEX-COVER, run on an instance with target size $k$ and $n$ vertices, has six stacks: the input $X$, the witness $W$, the counter $C$ (holding $k$), the counter $N$ (holding $n$), the vertex stack $V$ and its scratch stack $T$.
nodes.title: Stacks of the CLIQUE verifier

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a mode and $x$, $w$ bit lists. Suppose that $x$ decodes to $(k, n, \mathit{bits})$, that $w$ has at least $n$ bits, and that exactly $k$ of the first $n$ bits of $w$ are set. Then the verifier for mode $m$ on input $x$ and witness $w$ returns the same value as the row-by-row check for mode $m$ of the first $n$ bits of $w$ against the pair bits $\mathit{bits}$.
nodes.title: The verifier as a row-by-row check

nodes.summary: For a mode $m$ and bit lists $x$ and $w$, the verifier for mode $m$ accepts input $x$ with witness $w$ if and only if there are $k$, $n$ and a bit list $\mathit{bits}$ such that $x$ is the encoding of the instance $(k, n, \mathit{bits})$, $\mathit{bits}$ has one bit per pair $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$, $w$ has at least $n$ bits, exactly $k$ of the first $n$ bits of $w$ are set, and for all $i < j < n$ the pair…
nodes.title: Characterization of the CLIQUE verifier

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a mode, $k$ and $n$ natural numbers, let $\mathit{bits}$ be a bit list with one bit per pair $(i, j)$, $i < j < n$, and let $s$ be a set of $k$ vertices of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ that meets the pair condition of $m$ on every pair $i < j$. Then the verifier for mode $m$ accepts the encoding of $(k, n, \mathit{bits})$ with witness the characteristic vector of $s$: the list of $n$ bits whose $i$-th bit is…
nodes.title: The characteristic vector of a good vertex set is accepted

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a mode and $P$ a property of a number $k$ and a graph on $n$ vertices. Suppose that for all $n$, $k$ and every bit list $\mathit{bits}$ with one bit per pair $(i, j)$, $i < j < n$, the property $P$ holds for $k$ and the graph given by $\mathit{bits}$ exactly when some set of $k$ vertices meets the pair condition of $m$ on every pair $i < j$. Then for every bit list $x$, $x$ belongs to the language of…
nodes.title: Verifying a graph language defined by a vertex-set condition

nodes.summary: On an instance with target size $k$ and $n$ vertices, the verifier machine has the labels: read $k$, read $n$, load the witness, walk a row (carrying a bit $c$, the conjunction of the row's pair conditions so far), put the row back, accept, and reject.
nodes.title: Labels of the CLIQUE verifier

nodes.summary: Let $l$ be a list of pairs whose keys lie in a type with a lawful Boolean equality and are pairwise distinct. If $(a, b)$ occurs in $l$, then looking up the key $a$ in $l$ returns $b$.
nodes.title: Lookup in a list of pairs with distinct keys

nodes.summary: For every mode $m$ and all lists of bits $s$ and $b$, the row-by-row check of $s$ against $b$ holds if and only if $b$ has exactly one bit per pair $i < j < |s|$ and, listing these pairs in encoding order (rows $i$ ascending, within a row $j$ descending), the $t$-th pair $(i, j)$ and the $t$-th bit $b_t$ satisfy the pair condition $\mathrm{ok}_m(b_t, s_i, s_j)$ for every $t$.
nodes.title: The row-by-row check is the pairwise check

nodes.summary: For a mode $m$, a number $n$, a list of pair bits and a set $s$ of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, the set $s$ meets the condition of $m$ when for all vertices $i < j$ the pair condition $\mathrm{ok}_m(b_{ij}, [i \in s], [j \in s])$ holds, where $[i \in s]$ says whether $i$ is chosen and $b_{ij}$ is the bit of the pair $\{i, j\}$: listing the pairs $i' < j' < n$ in encoding order (rows $i'$ ascending, within a…
nodes.title: Vertex sets meeting a mode's pair condition

nodes.summary: If a bit list $w$ has length at least $n$, then the first $n$ entries of $w$ form the list $(w_0, \dots, w_{n-1})$, where $w_i$ is the entry of $w$ at index $i$ (taken as false past the end of $w$).
nodes.title: The first $n$ bits of a list, read index by index

nodes.summary: A bit string $x$ is in VERTEX-COVER if and only if there is a bit string $w$, no longer than $x$, such that the clique-family verifier in vertex-cover mode accepts $x$ with witness $w$.
nodes.title: VERTEX-COVER is verified by the clique verifier in cover mode
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
